sections.heading: Timely Vote Credits
paragraphs: Per the file, this design describes a (per the file) modification to the method (per the file) that is used to (per the file) calculate vote credits earned by node votes. Per the file, vote credits are the (per the file) accounting method used to (per the file) determine what percentage of inflation rewards a node earns on behalf of its stakers. Per the file, currently, when a slot that a node has previously voted on (per the file) is "rooted", it earns 1 vote credit. Per the file, a "rooted" slot is (per the file) one which has received (per the file) full commitment by the node (i.e. has been finalized). Per the file, one problem with this (per the file) simple accounting method is (per the file) that it awards one (per the file) credit regardless of how (per the file) "old" the slot that (per the file) was voted on at (per the file) the time that it was voted on.

Per the file, this means that a node can delay its voting for many slots so as to survey forks and (per the file) wait to make votes (per the file) that are less likely (per the file) to be expired, and (per the file) without incurring any penalty for doing so. Per the file, this is not just (per the file) a theoretical concern: there (per the file) are known and documented instances of nodes using this technique to (per the file) significantly delay their voting (per the file) while earning more credits as a result.

sections.heading: Proposed Change
paragraphs: The proposal is to (per the file) award a variable number (per the file) of vote credits per (per the file) voted on slot, with (per the file) more credits being given (per the file) for votes that have (per the file) "less latency" than votes (per the file) that have "more latency". Per the file, in this context, "latency" (per the file) is the number of (per the file) slots in between the (per the file) slot that is being (per the file) voted on and the (per the file) slot in which the vote has landed. Per the file, because a slot cannot (per the file) be voted on until (per the file) after it has been (per the file) completed, the minimum possible (per the file) latency is 1, which (per the file) would occur when a node voted as quickly as (per the file) possible, transmitting its vote (per the file) on that slot in (per the file) time for it to (per the file) be included in the very next slot.

Per the file, credits awarded would become (per the file) a function of this (per the file) latency, with lower latencies awarding more credits. Per the file, this will discourage intentional (per the file) "lagging", because delaying a (per the file) vote for any slots (per the file) decreases the number of (per the file) credits that vote will (per the file) earn, because it will (per the file) necessarily land in a (per the file) later slot if it (per the file) is delayed, and then (per the file) earn a lower number (per the file) of credits than it (per the file) would have earned had (per the file) it been transmitted immediately (per the file) and landed in an earlier slot. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Grace Period
paragraphs: Per the file, if landing a vote (per the file) with 1 slot latency (per the file) awarded more credit than (per the file) landing that same vote (per the file) in 2 slots latency, then nodes who could land votes (per the file) consistently within 1 slot (per the file) would have a credits (per the file) earning advantage over those who could not. Per the file, part of the latency (per the file) when transmitting votes is (per the file) unavoidable as it's a (per the file) function of geographical distance between (per the file) the sender and receiver of the vote. Per the file, the Solana network is (per the file) spread around the world (per the file) but it is not (per the file) evenly distributed over the (per the file) whole planet; there are (per the file) some locations which are, (per the file) on average, more distant (per the file) from the network than others are.

Per the file, it would likely be (per the file) harmful to the network (per the file) to encourage tight geographical concentration - if, as an illustration, the only way to (per the file) achieve 1 slot latency (per the file) was to be within (per the file) a specific country - then (per the file) a very strict credit (per the file) rewards schedule would encourage all nodes to move to the same country so as to maximize their credit earnings. Per the file, for this reason, the (per the file) credits reward schedule should (per the file) have a built-in "grace (per the file) period" that gives all nodes a "reasonable" amount of time (per the file) to land their votes. Per the file, this will reduce the (per the file) credits earning disadvantage that (per the file) comes from being more (per the file) distant from the network.

Per the file, a balance needs to (per the file) be struck between the (per the file) strictest rewards schedule, which (per the file) most strongly discourages intentional (per the file) lagging, and more lenient (per the file) rewards schedules, which improves (per the file) credit earnings for distant nodes who are not artificially lagging. Per the file, historical voting data has (per the file) been analyzed over many (per the file) epochs and the data (per the file) suggests that the smallest grace period that lets for very minimal impact (per the file) on well behaved distant nodes is 3 slots, which (per the file) means that all slots (per the file) voted on within 3 (per the file) slots will award maximum (per the file) vote credits to the voting node. Per the file, this gives nodes nearly 2 seconds to (per the file) land their votes without penalty.

Per the file, the maximum latency between (per the file) two points on Earth (per the file) is about 100 ms, (per the file) so allowing a full (per the file) 1,500 ms to 2,000 (per the file) ms latency without penalty should not (per the file) have adverse impact on distant nodes.

sections.heading: Maximum Vote Credits
paragraphs: Per the file, another factor to consider (per the file) is what the maximum (per the file) vote credits to award for a vote ought to be. Per the file, assuming linear reduction in (per the file) vote credits awarded (where (per the file) 1 slot of additional (per the file) lag reduces earned vote (per the file) credits by 1), the (per the file) maximum vote credits value (per the file) determines how much "penalty" (per the file) there is for each (per the file) additional slot of latency. Per the file, for example, a value (per the file) of 10 would mean (per the file) that after the grace (per the file) period slots, every additional (per the file) slot of latency would (per the file) result in a 10% (per the file) reduction in vote credits (per the file) earned as each subsequent (per the file) slot earns 1 credit (per the file) less out of a (per the file) maximum possible 10 credits.

Per the file, again, historical voting data (per the file) was analyzed over many (per the file) epochs and the conclusion (per the file) drawn was that a (per the file) maximum credits of 10 (per the file) is the largest value that may be used and still (per the file) have a noticeable effect on known laggers. Per the file, values higher than that (per the file) result in such a (per the file) small penalty for each (per the file) slot of lagging that (per the file) intentional lagging is still too profitable. Per the file, lower values are even (per the file) more punishing to intentional (per the file) lagging; but an attempt (per the file) has been made to (per the file) conservatively choose the highest (per the file) value that produces noticeable results.

Per the file, the selection of these (per the file) values is partially documented (per the file) here: https://www.shinobi-systems.com/timely_voting_proposal The above (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) document is somewhat out of date with more recent analysis, which occurred in this github issue: https://github.com/solana-labs/solana/issues/19002 To summarize the findings of these documents: analysis over many epochs showed that almost all nodes from all regions have an average vote latency of 1 slot or less. Per the file, the nodes with higher average latency (per the file) are either known laggers, (per the file) or are not representative (per the file) of their region since many other nodes in the same region (per the file) achieve low latency voting.

Per the file, with a maximum vote (per the file) credit of 10, there (per the file) is almost no change (per the file) in vote credits earned (per the file) relative to the highest (per the file) vote earner by the majority of nodes, aside from a general (per the file) uplift of about 0.4%.
